title: ProjectStory
text:
Introduction
In September 2023, New York City started enforcing Local Law 18, which made most short-term rentals like Airbnb illegal almost overnight. Hosts now have to register with the city, live in the unit, and rent to no more than two guests at a time. Within months, thousands of listings disappeared.
Supporters hoped those apartments would go back to long-term renters and ease one of the tightest rental markets in the country. This page follows that idea through Zillow’s rent data. I look at how rents moved before and after the law, which parts of the city changed the most, and whether related measures like renter demand and new listings shifted too. Finally, I ask how much of what followed can honestly be credited to the law, and how much would have happened anyway.

1. Rents before and after the law

county_zori %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = date, y = value, color = RegionName)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.Date("2023-09-01"), linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = as.Date("2023-09-01"), y = max(county_zori$value),
           label = "Local Law 18", hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Typical monthly rent", color = NULL,
       title = "Typical rent by county, 2021 to today") +
  theme_minimal()
